scenario: 面试题「设计一个像 YouTube 的视频推荐系统」,目录有数十亿视频,每次请求要在 sub-100ms 内返回。
scenario_en: The interview prompt 'design a YouTube-like video recommender' with billions of videos and a sub-100ms per-request budget.
q: 视频推荐的主流架构是什么，为什么要分两阶段？
q_en: What is the dominant video-recommendation architecture, and why two stages?
why: 主流是两阶段:候选生成(candidate generation)用轻量方法把数十亿→数百个,排序(ranking)用更重的模型给这数百个精细打分。单靠一个重模型给数十亿视频打分在 sub-100ms 内不可能,分层是为在延迟预算内兼顾规模与精度。
why_en: The dominant design is two stages: candidate generation narrows billions to hundreds with a light method, then ranking scores those hundreds with a heavier model, because scoring billions with one heavy model within sub-100ms is impossible.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["数十亿视频"] --> CG["候选生成
轻量, ANN"] CG --> H["数百候选"] H --> RK["排序
重模型精打分"] RK --> T["最终数十条"]
options: 单阶段:一个重模型直接给全部数十亿视频打分
两阶段:候选生成(轻量,billions→hundreds)+ 排序(重模型精打分),在延迟预算内兼顾规模与精度
两阶段:先排序全部视频,再随机采样候选
三阶段纯规则过滤,不用任何模型
options_en: Single stage: one heavy model scores all billions of videos directly.
Two stages: candidate generation (light, billions to hundreds) plus ranking (heavy, fine scoring), balancing scale and precision within the latency budget.
Two stages: rank all videos first, then randomly sample candidates.
Three stages of pure rule filtering with no models at all.
optionExplanations: 重模型给数十亿视频逐个打分在 sub-100ms 内根本跑不完,单阶段不可行。
对;轻量候选生成先收窄、重排序再精打分,是延迟预算下的标准两阶段解法。
顺序颠倒:排序是给少量候选精打分的,不可能先排全部再采样。
纯规则过滤无法个性化,也扛不住规模与质量要求。
optionExplanations_en: A heavy model scoring billions one by one cannot finish within sub-100ms, so a single stage is infeasible.
Correct — light candidate generation narrows first and heavy ranking scores precisely, the standard two-stage solution under a latency budget.
Order reversed: ranking scores a small candidate set, so you cannot rank everything first and then sample.
Pure rule filtering cannot personalize and cannot meet scale and quality requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段推荐的第一阶段,用轻量方法从海量目录快速筛出数百候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first stage of a two-stage recommender, using a light method to narrow a huge catalog to a few hundred candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段,用较重的模型给候选集精细打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is the second stage, scoring the candidate set finely with a heavier model.

scenario: 候选人一上来就画两塔、画排序模型框图,完全跳过了「这是给谁、优化什么、什么约束」的澄清。
scenario_en: A candidate immediately draws two-tower and ranking boxes, skipping any clarification of who it serves, what to optimize, and the constraints.
q: 为什么「先做问题框定再画框图」很重要，跳过它的后果是什么？
q_en: Why frame the problem before drawing boxes, and what happens if you skip it?
why: 问题框定决定了标签定义、指标、架构与约束——它是所有下游设计的地基。跳过它是这类题的头号失分点:你可能给错误的目标造了个漂亮系统,澄清问题才让每个设计决策有依据。
why_en: Problem framing fixes the label definition, metrics, architecture, and constraints — the foundation for every downstream choice — and skipping it is the number-one failure mode, since you may build an elegant system for the wrong objective.
options: 框定决定标签/指标/架构/约束,是下游设计地基;跳过=为错误目标造漂亮系统,是头号失分点
框定只是走流程,资深候选人可以直接跳到画架构
框定只跟商业无关的算法选择有关,与指标无关
跳过框定没有代价,只要架构图够漂亮就能通过
options_en: Framing fixes label/metrics/architecture/constraints, the foundation for downstream choices; skipping it builds an elegant system for the wrong objective — the top failure.
Framing is just procedure; senior candidates can jump straight to architecture.
Framing only concerns algorithm choices unrelated to business or metrics.
Skipping framing has no cost as long as the architecture diagram is pretty.
optionExplanations: 对;框定钉住目标与约束,后面每个决策才有依据,跳过它正是最常见的失分。
越资深越会花时间框定,因为它决定全局方向,不是可跳的形式。
框定恰恰把商业目标映射成 ML 指标,与指标定义紧密相关。
漂亮架构若对着错误目标就是白费,跳过框定代价极大。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — framing pins the objective and constraints so every later decision has a basis, and skipping it is the most common way to lose points.
More senior candidates spend more time framing because it sets global direction; it is not a skippable formality.
Framing precisely maps business goals to ML metrics and is tightly tied to metric definition.
A pretty architecture aimed at the wrong objective is wasted, so skipping framing is very costly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 画架构前先澄清目标、用户、约束、指标,把业务问题翻译成 ML 问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem framing clarifies objective, users, constraints, and metrics before architecture, translating a business problem into an ML one.

scenario: 澄清产品形态:这个推荐是首页 feed(用户刚进来、没有明确上下文),还是「看完这个接着看」的侧边栏(有当前正在看的视频作锚)。
scenario_en: Clarify the surface: is this a homepage feed (user just arrived, no explicit context) or a watch-next sidebar (anchored to the currently playing video)?
q: 首页 feed vs watch-next 侧边栏这个区分，主要驱动哪个下游设计决策？
q_en: Homepage feed vs watch-next sidebar mainly drives which downstream design decision?
why: 它决定候选生成的策略:首页 feed 没有当前视频锚点,要做宽主题的候选生成(覆盖用户广泛兴趣);watch-next 有正在看的视频作锚,要做上下文锚定的候选生成(与当前视频强相关)。
why_en: It drives the candidate-generation strategy: a homepage feed has no anchor and needs broad-topic candidate generation, while a watch-next sidebar is anchored to the current video and needs contextually-anchored generation.
tradeoff: 宽主题候选生成(首页、覆盖广兴趣) vs 上下文锚定候选生成(watch-next、强相关当前视频)
options: 决定用什么数据库存视频元数据
决定候选生成策略:首页 feed→宽主题;watch-next→上下文锚定当前视频
决定前端用什么框架渲染
决定模型用几张 GPU 训练
options_en: Which database stores video metadata.
The candidate-generation strategy: homepage feed to broad-topic, watch-next to context-anchored on the current video.
Which frontend framework renders the UI.
How many GPUs train the model.
whenOtherWins: 若产品其实是纯搜索结果页(用户已输入明确 query),候选生成就该由 query 驱动,而非 feed 的兴趣覆盖或 watch-next 的视频锚定。
whenOtherWins_en: If the surface is actually a search results page with an explicit query, candidate generation should be query-driven, not feed interest coverage or watch-next anchoring.
optionExplanations: 选数据库是存储层细节,与「有没有当前视频锚点」这个产品语义无关。
对;有无锚点直接决定候选生成是宽主题还是上下文锚定,这是产品澄清的核心影响。
前端框架与推荐候选策略无关,答不到设计影响。
GPU 数量是训练资源,不由产品形态的锚点差异决定。
optionExplanations_en: Choosing a database is a storage detail, unrelated to the product semantics of whether there is a current-video anchor.
Correct — presence of an anchor directly decides broad-topic vs context-anchored candidate generation, the core impact of this product clarification.
The frontend framework is unrelated to candidate strategy and misses the design impact.
GPU count is a training resource, not decided by the anchor difference in product surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以当前正在播放的视频为上下文锚点,推荐紧接着看的视频。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watch-next uses the currently playing video as a context anchor to recommend what to watch next.

scenario: 澄清用户:目标用户是已登录(有丰富观看历史)还是匿名(几乎没有个人历史)。
scenario_en: Clarify the user: are targets logged-in (rich watch history) or anonymous (almost no personal history)?
q: 登录 vs 匿名这个区分，主要驱动哪个设计决策？
q_en: Logged-in vs anonymous mainly drives which design decision?
why: 它决定用协同过滤还是内容信号,以及要不要处理冷启动:登录用户有历史,可用协同过滤(看过 X 的人也看 Y);匿名用户没历史,得靠内容特征/上下文,面对冷启动问题。
why_en: It decides collaborative filtering vs content-based signals and whether you handle cold start: logged-in users have history for collaborative filtering, while anonymous users lack history and need content/context signals under cold start.
tradeoff: 协同过滤(需历史、登录用户) vs 内容/上下文信号(无历史、匿名/冷启动)
options: 决定视频用什么编码格式存储
决定 CDN 节点部署在哪里
决定用协同过滤还是内容信号 + 要不要处理冷启动:登录有历史用 CF,匿名无历史靠内容/上下文
决定排序模型的学习率大小
options_en: Which codec stores the videos.
Where CDN nodes are deployed.
Collaborative filtering vs content signals plus whether to handle cold start: logged-in has history for CF, anonymous lacks it and uses content/context.
The ranking model's learning rate.
whenOtherWins: 若即便登录用户也普遍缺历史(新平台早期),那所有人都近似冷启动,应主打内容信号而非协同过滤。
whenOtherWins_en: If even logged-in users mostly lack history (an early-stage platform), everyone is near cold start and you should lead with content signals over collaborative filtering.
optionExplanations: 编码格式是存储/播放细节,与用户有无历史的建模选择无关。
CDN 部署是分发层,不由「登录 vs 匿名」的信号可得性决定。
对;有无历史直接决定 CF vs 内容信号与冷启动处理,是用户澄清的核心影响。
学习率是训练超参,不由用户是否登录这个产品语义决定。
optionExplanations_en: Codec is a storage/playback detail, unrelated to the modeling choice of whether the user has history.
CDN deployment is a delivery-layer concern, not decided by logged-in vs anonymous signal availability.
Correct — history availability directly decides CF vs content signals and cold-start handling, the core impact of this user clarification.
Learning rate is a training hyperparameter, not decided by the product semantics of logged-in status.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据行为相似的用户群推荐:看过 X 的人也看 Y,需要用户历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends from behaviorally similar users (people who watched X also watched Y), needing user history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品缺历史时无法用协同过滤,需内容/上下文兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a new user or item lacks history so collaborative filtering fails and content/context must fill in.

scenario: 澄清内容规模:目录到底是几千个视频,还是数十亿个视频。
scenario_en: Clarify catalog scale: is it a few thousand videos or billions?
q: 目录规模这个澄清，主要决定哪个架构选择？
q_en: The catalog-scale clarification mainly decides which architecture choice?
why: 它决定候选生成阶段要不要上 ANN 检索:目录小可以暴力打分或简单过滤;数十亿量级无法逐个打分,必须用近似最近邻(ANN)在预算内把 billions 收窄到 hundreds。
why_en: It decides whether candidate generation needs ANN retrieval: a small catalog can be brute-force scored, but billions cannot be scored one by one and require approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search to narrow within budget.
tradeoff: 小目录(暴力/简单过滤够用) vs 数十亿目录(必须 ANN 检索)
options: 决定用什么日志系统
决定候选生成要不要上 ANN 检索:小目录可暴力打分,数十亿必须用近似最近邻
决定 A/B 实验分几组
决定用户界面配色
options_en: Which logging system to use.
Whether candidate generation needs ANN retrieval: a small catalog can be brute-force scored, billions require approximate nearest neighbor.
How many groups the A/B test uses.
The UI color scheme.
whenOtherWins: 若目录只有几千条,ANN 是过度工程,直接暴力打分或简单启发式过滤更省事、还没有近似召回损失。
whenOtherWins_en: If the catalog is only a few thousand, ANN is over-engineering — brute-force scoring or a simple heuristic filter is simpler with no approximation recall loss.
optionExplanations: 日志系统是可观测性细节,与候选检索是否需要 ANN 无关。
对;规模是否到数十亿直接决定能否暴力打分,还是必须 ANN,这是内容澄清的核心。
A/B 分组是实验设计,不由目录规模决定。
配色是前端,与检索架构无关。
optionExplanations_en: A logging system is an observability detail, unrelated to whether retrieval needs ANN.
Correct — whether scale reaches billions directly decides brute-force vs mandatory ANN, the core of this content clarification.
A/B grouping is experiment design, not decided by catalog scale.
Color scheme is frontend, unrelated to retrieval architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索:牺牲一点精确度换取在海量向量里毫秒级找到相近项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search trades a little exactness for millisecond retrieval of nearby items among massive vectors.

scenario: 澄清优化目标:主要优化「观看时长」这种即时参与,还是「长期满意度/留存」这种慢变量。
scenario_en: Clarify the objective: optimize immediate engagement like watch time, or a slow variable like long-term satisfaction/retention?
q: 优化目标的澄清，主要决定哪些下游 ML 设计？
q_en: The objective clarification mainly decides which downstream ML choices?
why: 它决定标签定义、损失函数和护栏指标:优化观看时长就以预测观看时长为标签/损失;要长期满意度则得引入 7 天回访等慢标签,并配护栏指标防止只追即时参与把体验带偏。
why_en: It decides label definition, loss function, and guardrail metric: optimizing watch time makes predicted watch time the label/loss, while long-term satisfaction needs slow labels like 7-day repeat visits plus a guardrail so chasing engagement does not wreck experience.
tradeoff: 观看时长(即时、易测但易诱导标题党) vs 长期满意度(慢标签但护住留存)
options: 决定标签定义/损失函数/护栏指标:优化观看时长以预测时长为标签,长期满意度需慢标签+护栏防跑偏
只决定用哪家云厂商
只决定视频缩略图尺寸
只决定缓存过期时间
options_en: Label definition/loss/guardrail: optimizing watch time makes predicted time the label, while long-term satisfaction needs slow labels plus a guardrail.
Only which cloud vendor to use.
Only the thumbnail size.
Only the cache expiry time.
whenOtherWins: 若产品明确只追短期变现(如广告位测试),可暂时只用观看时长做标签,但仍应挂个护栏指标监控长期体验。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product explicitly chases short-term monetization (an ad-slot test), you may temporarily use watch time alone as the label, but still attach a guardrail to watch long-term experience.
optionExplanations: 对;目标直接决定标签、损失和护栏,是把商业目标翻译成 ML 问题的关键澄清。
云厂商是基建选型,与优化目标的标签定义无关。
缩略图尺寸是产品细节,不由优化目标决定。
缓存过期是工程参数,与标签/损失/护栏无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the objective directly decides label, loss, and guardrail, the key clarification translating business goals into an ML problem.
Cloud vendor is infrastructure selection, unrelated to the objective's label definition.
Thumbnail size is a product detail, not decided by the objective.
Cache expiry is an engineering parameter, unrelated to label/loss/guardrail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与主目标并列监控的副指标,防止一味优化主目标损害长期体验(如多样性、留存)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a secondary metric watched alongside the primary objective to prevent over-optimizing it from harming long-term experience.

scenario: 澄清约束:端到端延迟预算是宽松(几百 ms 可接受)还是紧张(必须 sub-100ms)。
scenario_en: Clarify constraints: is the end-to-end latency budget loose (a few hundred ms) or tight (sub-100ms)?
q: 延迟预算这个约束，主要决定哪个架构取舍？
q_en: The latency-budget constraint mainly decides which architectural tradeoff?
why: 它决定实时排序 vs 预计算:预算宽松可以在请求时跑更重的实时模型;预算紧张(sub-100ms)则很多计算得预先算好(如视频侧嵌入离线预计算),把在线只留下最省的那部分。
why_en: It decides real-time ranking vs precomputation: a loose budget allows a heavier real-time model at request time, while a tight sub-100ms budget forces precomputing much of the work (e.g. offline video embeddings) so only the cheapest part runs online.
tradeoff: 实时计算(灵活、新鲜但吃延迟预算) vs 预计算(省在线延迟但牺牲新鲜度/灵活性)
options: 决定用什么编程语言写服务
决定实时排序 vs 预计算:紧预算(sub-100ms)迫使大量计算预先算好,在线只留最省部分
决定招几个工程师
决定日志保留多少天
options_en: Which programming language the service uses.
Real-time ranking vs precomputation: a tight sub-100ms budget forces precomputing much of the work, leaving only the cheapest part online.
How many engineers to hire.
How many days logs are retained.
whenOtherWins: 若延迟预算宽松(离线批量推荐邮件、无需秒回),可以在请求时跑更重的实时模型换取更高精度,不必大量预计算。
whenOtherWins_en: If the latency budget is loose (offline batch recommendation emails with no instant response), run a heavier real-time model at request time for accuracy instead of heavy precomputation.
optionExplanations: 编程语言是实现细节,不由端到端延迟预算这个架构约束决定。
对;预算松紧直接决定哪些算实时、哪些预计算,是约束澄清的核心影响。
招聘是团队问题,与延迟预算的架构取舍无关。
日志保留是运维策略,与实时 vs 预计算无关。
optionExplanations_en: Programming language is an implementation detail, not decided by the end-to-end latency constraint.
Correct — how tight the budget is directly decides what runs real-time vs precomputed, the core impact of this constraint clarification.
Hiring is a team question, unrelated to the latency budget's architectural tradeoff.
Log retention is an ops policy, unrelated to real-time vs precomputation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把耗时计算提前离线算好存起来,在线只做最轻的查询,以压低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precomputation does expensive work offline in advance and stores it, so online only does light lookups to cut latency.

scenario: 澄清是否采集负反馈:系统要不要记录 skip、dislike 这类「用户不喜欢」的信号。
scenario_en: Clarify negative-feedback capture: does the system log skips/dislikes — signals of what users don't want?
q: 是否采集负反馈这个澄清，主要决定训练数据的什么？
q_en: The negative-feedback clarification mainly decides what about the training data?
why: 它决定训练数据是否含负信号:采集 skip/dislike 就能同时用正负样本训练;不采集就只有正样本(仅点击),模型会把「没点击」当中性,误读意图、强化低质推荐。
why_en: It decides whether training data includes negative signals: capturing skips/dislikes lets you train on both positive and negative samples, while positive-only (clicks) makes the model treat no-click as neutral, misreading intent.
tradeoff: 含负反馈(正负样本、更准建模不喜欢) vs 仅正反馈(把无点击当中性、易误读意图)
options: 决定训练数据含不含负信号:采集 skip/dislike→正负样本;只正样本→把无点击当中性、误读意图
只决定视频清晰度
只决定推荐条数
只决定服务器机房位置
options_en: Whether training data includes negative signals: capturing skips/dislikes gives positive+negative samples; positive-only treats no-click as neutral, misreading intent.
Only video resolution.
Only the number of recommendations.
Only the server datacenter location.
whenOtherWins: 若平台确实几乎没有可靠的负反馈渠道(如纯浏览无交互按钮),只能先用正样本+采样负例近似,但要显式承认这个偏差。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform truly lacks reliable negative channels (pure browsing with no interaction buttons), you may approximate with positives plus sampled negatives, but explicitly acknowledge the bias.
optionExplanations: 对;采不采负反馈直接决定训练能否用负样本,是最容易被忽略却很关键的澄清。
清晰度是播放质量,与训练标签正负无关。
推荐条数是产品参数,不由负反馈采集决定。
机房位置是基建,与训练数据的正负信号无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — whether you capture negative feedback directly decides whether training can use negative samples, an easily overlooked but crucial clarification.
Resolution is playback quality, unrelated to positive/negative training labels.
The number of recommendations is a product parameter, not decided by negative-feedback capture.
Datacenter location is infrastructure, unrelated to positive/negative training signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户不喜欢的信号(skip、dislike),让模型学到「不该推什么」,而非只学正样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative feedback is signals of dislike (skip, dislike) that teach the model what not to recommend, not just positives.

scenario: 一个推荐系统只从正向参与(点击、观看)学习,把「用户没点」一律当作中性、无信息。
scenario_en: A recommender learns only from positive engagement (clicks, watches) and treats every no-click as neutral and uninformative.
q: 「只学正反馈、把无点击当中性」会导致什么后果链？
q_en: What consequence chain follows from 'learn only from positives, treat no-click as neutral'?
why: 只学正样本→把「没点」误当中性而非负信号→误读用户意图(其实是不喜欢)→继续推类似低质内容→正反馈回路自我强化,质量悄悄下滑。修法是显式建模负反馈(skip/dislike)。
why_en: Positive-only training treats no-click as neutral rather than negative, misreads intent, keeps recommending similar low-quality content, and self-reinforces via the feedback loop, quietly degrading quality — fixed by explicitly modeling negatives.
options: 无点击当中性→误读意图→继续推类似低质内容→正反馈回路自我强化、质量下滑;修法是建模负反馈
毫无影响,正样本足够学到完整偏好
只会让训练更快收敛,是优点
会导致 GPU 过热,是硬件问题
options_en: No-click as neutral misreads intent, keeps recommending similar low-quality content, self-reinforces via the loop, and degrades quality; fix by modeling negatives.
No effect; positives suffice to learn full preferences.
It only makes training converge faster, a benefit.
It overheats the GPU, a hardware problem.
optionExplanations: 对;把负信号当中性抹掉了「不喜欢」,回路会不断强化低质推荐,必须显式建模负反馈。
正样本缺了「不喜欢」的一半信息,学不到完整偏好,并非无影响。
收敛快但学错了目标,把误读意图当优点是本末倒置。
GPU 过热与训练信号正负毫无关系,是无关项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — treating negatives as neutral erases 'dislike', and the loop keeps reinforcing low-quality recs, so negatives must be modeled explicitly.
Positives lack the 'dislike' half, so full preferences cannot be learned — not a no-op.
Fast convergence toward the wrong objective is not a benefit; calling misread intent an advantage is backwards.
GPU overheating has nothing to do with positive/negative training signal, an irrelevant option.

termDefinitions.term: positive-only bias / 仅正样本偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 只用正向参与训练,把无交互误当中性,导致意图误读与低质自我强化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Positive-only bias trains only on positive engagement and mistakes no-interaction for neutral, causing intent misreading and low-quality self-reinforcement.

scenario: 商业目标是最大化广告收入,而观看时长是最直接的广告收入驱动。
scenario_en: The business goal is maximizing ad revenue, and watch time is the most direct driver of ad revenue.
q: 该把这个商业目标映射成哪个 ML 排序信号？
q_en: Which ML ranking signal should this business goal map to?
why: 映射成预测观看时长(predicted watch time)作排序信号:观看时长最直接驱动广告收入,让模型学着把预计看得更久的视频排上去。但要配护栏,否则会滑向标题党。
why_en: Map it to predicted watch time as the ranking signal: watch time most directly drives ad revenue, so the model learns to rank videos users will watch longer — but pair it with a guardrail or it slides toward clickbait.
tradeoff: 预测观看时长(直连广告收入但易诱导标题党) vs 纯点击(易被缩略图党刷,更浅)
options: 映射成预测点击率,忽略看多久
映射成预测观看时长作排序信号:最直接驱动广告收入,需配护栏防标题党
映射成视频文件大小
映射成上传时间新旧
options_en: Map to predicted click-through rate, ignoring how long they watch.
Map to predicted watch time as the ranking signal: most directly drives ad revenue, paired with a guardrail against clickbait.
Map to video file size.
Map to upload recency.
whenOtherWins: 若目标其实是「让用户尽快找到想要的」(如客服短视频),预测点击/首屏满足度比观看时长更贴合,时长长反而可能是没找到。
whenOtherWins_en: If the goal is 'help users find what they want fast' (support clips), predicted click/first-screen satisfaction fits better than watch time, where long watch may mean they didn't find it.
optionExplanations: 纯点击只看点没点、看不到看多久,和「观看时长驱动广告收入」的目标不匹配。
对;预测观看时长最直连广告收入,是这个商业目标的标准 ML 映射,记得配护栏。
文件大小与用户是否爱看无关,不能当排序目标。
上传新旧是一个特征,不是要优化的商业目标。
optionExplanations_en: Pure clicks capture whether they clicked, not how long they watched, mismatching the watch-time-drives-revenue goal.
Correct — predicted watch time most directly connects to ad revenue, the standard ML mapping for this business goal, with a guardrail.
File size is unrelated to whether users enjoy it and cannot be a ranking target.
Upload recency is a feature, not the business objective to optimize.

termDefinitions.term: predicted watch time / 预测观看时长
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预估用户会看某视频多久,作为直连广告收入的排序信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predicted watch time is the model's estimate of how long a user will watch a video, a ranking signal directly tied to ad revenue.

scenario: 商业目标是提升用户长期满意度(用 7 天回访、问卷、正负交互比来代理),你关心「最让人满意的视频有没有排在靠前」。
scenario_en: The goal is long-term user satisfaction (proxied by 7-day repeat visits, surveys, positive/negative interaction ratio), and you care whether the most satisfying videos rank near the top.
q: 该用哪个 ML 指标来衡量排序质量？
q_en: Which ML metric measures this ranking quality?
why: 用 NDCG:它对排序位置加权(越靠前贡献越大),正好衡量「最让人满意的视频是否排在前面」。满意度是慢变量,用 7 天回访等代理喂给 NDCG 评估排序好坏。
why_en: Use NDCG: it weights by rank position (higher positions count more), directly measuring whether the most satisfying videos sit near the top, with satisfaction proxied by 7-day repeat visits.
tradeoff: NDCG(位置加权、重排序顺序) vs Recall@K(只看有没有召回、不看顺序)
options: 用 Recall@K:只看相关视频有没有进候选集,不看排位
用准确率 accuracy:是否分类正确
用 NDCG:位置加权,衡量最满意的视频是否排在靠前
用 QPS:每秒查询数
options_en: Use Recall@K: only whether relevant videos entered the candidate set, ignoring rank.
Use accuracy: whether classification is correct.
Use NDCG: position-weighted, measuring whether the most satisfying videos rank near the top.
Use QPS: queries per second.
whenOtherWins: 若评估的是候选生成阶段(只关心相关视频有没有被召回、还没排序),那 Recall@K 比 NDCG 更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If evaluating candidate generation (only whether relevant videos were retrieved, not yet ranked), Recall@K fits better than NDCG.
optionExplanations: Recall@K 只管有没有召回,不管排在第几,答不了「满意视频是否靠前」。
accuracy 是分类指标,不衡量排序顺序质量。
对;NDCG 位置加权,正好评估最满意内容是否排前,匹配满意度目标。
QPS 是吞吐量指标,与排序质量无关。
optionExplanations_en: Recall@K only cares whether it was retrieved, not at what rank, so it cannot answer whether satisfying videos are near the top.
Accuracy is a classification metric and does not measure ranking-order quality.
Correct — NDCG is position-weighted and evaluates whether the most satisfying content ranks high, matching the satisfaction goal.
QPS is a throughput metric, unrelated to ranking quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益:按排位加权的排序质量指标,越靠前的相关项贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a rank-weighted ranking-quality metric where relevant items nearer the top contribute more.

scenario: 商业目标是保护内容多样性——护住创作者生态、避免用户被困在信息茧房(filter bubble)。
scenario_en: The goal is protecting content diversity — safeguarding the creator ecosystem and avoiding filter bubbles.
q: 该用哪些 ML 指标来衡量多样性？
q_en: Which ML metrics measure diversity?
why: 用覆盖率(coverage:被推荐过的目录占比)衡量整体多样性,配列表内多样性(intra-list diversity:单次推荐列表内部够不够多元)。二者共同护住创作者生态与防茧房,常作为观看时长目标的护栏。
why_en: Use coverage (fraction of the catalog ever recommended) for overall diversity plus intra-list diversity (how varied a single recommendation list is), together guarding the creator ecosystem and against filter bubbles, often as a guardrail on watch time.
tradeoff: 覆盖率+列表内多样性(护生态、防茧房) vs 纯观看时长(集中头部、窄化)
options: 覆盖率(被推过的目录占比)+ 列表内多样性,共同护创作者生态与防茧房
只用观看时长,时长高就代表多样
只用 p99 延迟衡量多样性
用模型参数量衡量多样性
options_en: Coverage (fraction of catalog ever recommended) plus intra-list diversity, together guarding the creator ecosystem and against filter bubbles.
Just watch time; high watch time means diversity.
Just p99 latency to measure diversity.
Model parameter count to measure diversity.
whenOtherWins: 若产品阶段目标是极致精准的窄推荐(如专业教程连播),暂时可弱化多样性护栏,但要监控长期茧房与创作者流失风险。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product phase targets ultra-precise narrow recommendations (a specialized tutorial series), you may relax the diversity guardrail temporarily but monitor long-term filter-bubble and creator-churn risk.
optionExplanations: 对;覆盖率+列表内多样性正是衡量多样性的两个互补维度,护生态又防茧房。
观看时长高常常来自集中推头部,反而与多样性对立,不能代表多样。
延迟是性能指标,与内容多样性毫无关系。
参数量是模型规模,与推荐多样性无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — coverage plus intra-list diversity are two complementary diversity dimensions, guarding the ecosystem and against bubbles.
High watch time often comes from concentrating on head content, opposing diversity, so it cannot represent it.
Latency is a performance metric with nothing to do with content diversity.
Parameter count is model size, unrelated to recommendation diversity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 目录中曾被推荐过的视频占比,衡量整体推荐多样性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the fraction of the catalog ever recommended, measuring overall recommendation diversity.

termDefinitions.term: intra-list diversity / 列表内多样性
termDefinitions.meaning: 单个推荐列表内部内容彼此差异程度,越同质越低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Intra-list diversity is how different the items within a single recommendation list are from each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐只喂相似内容,把用户困在越来越窄的兴趣圈里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A filter bubble is when recommendations feed only similar content, trapping the user in an ever-narrowing interest circle.

scenario: 在一个数十亿视频的系统里,你要评估候选生成阶段做得好不好——它负责把 billions 收窄成 hundreds 交给排序。
scenario_en: In a billions-of-videos system, evaluate how well candidate generation does — it narrows billions to hundreds for ranking.
q: 评估候选生成阶段，最合适的指标是什么？
q_en: What is the best metric to evaluate the candidate generation stage?
why: 用 Recall@K(前 K 个候选里覆盖了多少真正相关视频):候选生成的职责是检索完整性——一个没进候选集的视频永远没机会被排序。所以这一阶段看召回而非排序顺序。
why_en: Use Recall@K (how many truly relevant videos appear in the top-K candidates): candidate generation's job is retrieval completeness, since a video not in the candidate set can never be ranked, so measure recall not order.
tradeoff: Recall@K(候选阶段、看召回完整性) vs NDCG(排序阶段、看位置质量)
options: 用 p99 延迟
用 NDCG,因为要看排序顺序
用点击率 CTR
用 Recall@K:候选生成看检索完整性,没进候选集的视频永远无法被排序
options_en: Use p99 latency.
Use NDCG because you care about ranking order.
Use click-through rate CTR.
Use Recall@K: candidate generation is about retrieval completeness, since a video not in the set can never be ranked.
whenOtherWins: 到了排序阶段,相关视频已在候选集里,这时要看它们排得对不对,该换成位置加权的 NDCG 而非 Recall@K。
whenOtherWins_en: At the ranking stage the relevant videos are already in the set, so you care whether they are ordered well and switch to position-weighted NDCG instead of Recall@K.
optionExplanations: 延迟是性能约束,不衡量候选集有没有把相关视频捞全。
NDCG 衡量排序顺序,但候选生成阶段还没排序,重点是召回而非顺序。
CTR 是参与度指标,评估不了候选检索的完整性。
对;候选生成的成败在于相关视频有没有被召回进集合,Recall@K 正是这个。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is a performance constraint and does not measure whether the set captured all relevant videos.
NDCG measures ranking order, but candidate generation is not yet ranking, so recall matters more than order.
CTR is an engagement metric and cannot evaluate retrieval completeness of candidates.
Correct — candidate generation succeeds or fails on whether relevant videos got retrieved into the set, which Recall@K captures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前 K 个候选里覆盖了多少真正相关的视频,衡量候选生成的检索完整性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K measures how many truly relevant videos are covered in the top-K candidates, gauging candidate-generation retrieval completeness.

scenario: 团队决定纯粹优化「预测观看时长」这一个目标,没有任何护栏指标。
scenario_en: The team decides to purely optimize the single objective 'predicted watch time' with no guardrail metric.
q: 只追单一观看时长目标、不设护栏，会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you chase watch time alone with no guardrail?
why: 会滑向标题党/诱导内容,并形成自我强化的反馈回路:模型学到什么留住人就多推什么,logged 数据又强化它,最终训练-服务偏差让质量悄悄退化。所以要在主目标旁并置护栏指标(多样性/满意度)。
why_en: It slides toward clickbait and a self-reinforcing feedback loop: the model recommends whatever retains, logged data reinforces it, and training-serving skew silently degrades quality, so place a guardrail (diversity/satisfaction) beside the primary objective.
options: 毫无风险,单目标最干净
滑向标题党+自我强化反馈回路(训练-服务偏差),质量悄悄退化;须并置护栏指标
只会提升多样性,是意外好处
会降低广告收入,与观看时长无关
options_en: No risk; a single objective is cleanest.
Slides toward clickbait plus a self-reinforcing feedback loop (training-serving skew), silently degrading quality; place a guardrail metric alongside.
It only boosts diversity, an accidental benefit.
It lowers ad revenue, unrelated to watch time.
optionExplanations: 单目标看似干净实则危险:没有护栏就会被观看时长这一维度带偏,牺牲长期体验。
对;纯观看时长会诱导标题党并经反馈回路自我强化,护栏指标是必备的平衡。
纯观看时长通常降低多样性(集中头部),不会意外提升。
观看时长恰恰驱动广告收入,单优化短期反而抬收入、伤长期,不是降收入。
optionExplanations_en: A single objective looks clean but is dangerous: with no guardrail, the watch-time dimension skews it and sacrifices long-term experience.
Correct — pure watch time invites clickbait and self-reinforces via the loop, so a guardrail metric is the necessary balance.
Pure watch time usually lowers diversity (concentrating on head content), not accidentally raising it.
Watch time drives ad revenue, so optimizing it alone raises short-term revenue while harming the long term, not lowering revenue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠夸张标题/缩略图诱导点击但内容低质,纯观看时长优化易奖励它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clickbait uses sensational titles/thumbnails to lure clicks with low-quality content, which pure watch-time optimization tends to reward.

scenario: 面试官问你两阶段各用什么指标,想看你能否把「检索完整性」和「排序质量」分清。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which metric fits each stage, checking whether you separate retrieval completeness from ranking quality.
q: Recall@K 和 NDCG 分别评估两阶段的什么，核心区别是什么？
q_en: What do Recall@K and NDCG each evaluate across the two stages, and what is the core difference?
why: Recall@K 评估候选生成的检索完整性——相关视频有没有被捞进候选集,不管排第几;NDCG 评估排序阶段的位置质量——相关视频排得够不够靠前。前者只问「有没有」,后者问「排得对不对」。
why_en: Recall@K evaluates candidate generation's retrieval completeness (did relevant videos enter the set, regardless of rank), while NDCG evaluates ranking's position quality (are relevant videos near the top) — presence versus ordering.
tradeoff: Recall@K(候选阶段、只问有没有召回) vs NDCG(排序阶段、问排得对不对)
options: 两者都评估排序阶段,只是公式不同
Recall@K 评候选生成的检索完整性(只问有没有召回);NDCG 评排序的位置质量(排得对不对)
Recall@K 评排序、NDCG 评候选生成
两者都只用于离线,线上不能用
options_en: Both evaluate the ranking stage, just with different formulas.
Recall@K evaluates candidate-generation retrieval completeness (presence); NDCG evaluates ranking position quality (ordering).
Recall@K evaluates ranking and NDCG evaluates candidate generation.
Both are offline-only and cannot be used online.
optionExplanations: 两者对应不同阶段:一个候选生成一个排序,不是都评排序。
对;检索完整性 vs 位置质量,正好切开两阶段各自的成功判据。
说反了:Recall@K 对应候选生成,NDCG 对应排序。
两者离线在线都可评估,不存在只能离线的限制。
optionExplanations_en: They map to different stages — one to candidate generation, one to ranking — not both to ranking.
Correct — retrieval completeness vs position quality cleanly splits each stage's success criterion.
Backwards: Recall@K maps to candidate generation and NDCG to ranking.
Both can be evaluated offline and online; there is no offline-only restriction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相关物品有没有被候选生成捞进集合,是候选阶段的成功判据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval completeness is whether relevant items got pulled into the set by candidate generation, the success criterion of that stage.

scenario: 系统规模:数十亿视频、数十亿账号、数亿 DAU;每个会话有几十次请求,每次端到端要在 sub-100ms 内返回。
scenario_en: Scale: billions of videos and accounts, hundreds of millions of DAU; each session has dozens of requests, each returning end-to-end within sub-100ms.
q: 「sub-100ms 端到端」这个数字在设计里该怎么用？
q_en: How should the 'sub-100ms end-to-end' number be used in design?
why: sub-100ms 是给定的产品级 SLO(不是公式推出来的),它约束的是架构路径:总预算要拆给候选生成(~10-20ms)、排序(~50-80ms)、特征查询(单位数 ms),任何来不及查的特征必须预计算或丢弃。考的是这个数字逼出的架构,而非背数字本身。
why_en: Sub-100ms is a given product-level SLO (not derived), and it constrains the architecture path: the budget splits across candidate generation (~10-20ms), ranking (~50-80ms), and feature lookups (single-digit ms), so any feature too slow to fetch must be precomputed or dropped.
options: sub-100ms 是要背下来的硬数字,考点就是记住 100
sub-100ms 说明不用两阶段,单模型也够快
sub-100ms 是给定 SLO:约束把预算拆给候选生成~10-20ms/排序~50-80ms/特征查询单位数 ms,慢特征须预计算或丢弃
sub-100ms 只影响前端动画,不影响后端架构
options_en: sub-100ms is a hard number to memorize; the point is remembering 100.
sub-100ms means two stages are unnecessary; a single model is fast enough.
sub-100ms is a given SLO: it splits the budget across candidate generation ~10-20ms / ranking ~50-80ms / feature lookups single-digit ms, and slow features must be precomputed or dropped.
sub-100ms only affects frontend animation, not backend architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务水平目标:给定的延迟/可用性目标,是约束而非公式结果,用来倒逼架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given latency/availability target — a constraint, not a formula result — used to drive architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数,衡量规模的基数,影响吞吐与容量估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU (Daily Active Users) is the daily active user count, a scale base affecting throughput and capacity estimates.

It commits the design to this assumption: sub-100ms only affects frontend animation, not backend architecture.

scenario: 候选生成阶段要在大约 10-20ms 内把数十亿视频收窄到数百个。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must narrow billions of videos to hundreds within roughly 10-20ms.
q: 这个「10-20ms 内 billions→hundreds」的预算逼出什么架构选择？
q_en: What architecture does the '10-20ms, billions to hundreds' budget force?
why: 10-20ms 内不可能给数十亿视频逐个打分,所以必须用近似最近邻(ANN)检索或预过滤:把视频预先编码成向量存进 ANN 索引,查询时用用户向量近邻检索,毫秒级返回数百候选。这就是为什么候选生成用双塔+ANN 而非逐个打分。
why_en: Scoring billions in 10-20ms is impossible, so you need ANN search or pre-filtered retrieval: precompute video vectors into an ANN index and query with the user vector for millisecond top-hundreds retrieval, which is why candidate generation uses two-tower plus ANN, not per-item scoring.
options: 逼出 ANN 检索/预过滤:视频预编码入 ANN 索引,查询用户向量近邻检索,毫秒级返回数百候选
逼出用一个大 Transformer 实时给每个视频打分
逼出把所有视频加载进内存逐个遍历
逼出关闭个性化、只推全局热门
options_en: Forces ANN retrieval/pre-filtering: precompute video vectors into an ANN index and query with the user vector for millisecond top-hundreds.
Forces one big Transformer to score every video in real time.
Forces loading all videos into memory and iterating one by one.
Forces disabling personalization and recommending only global trending.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量条件(向量近邻/规则)快速圈出小候选集,再交给下游,避免逐个打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-filtered retrieval quickly narrows to a small candidate set with light conditions (vector nearest-neighbor/rules) before downstream, avoiding per-item scoring.

选项主张：逼出用一个大 Transformer 实时给每个视频打分。

scenario: 排序模型想用某个特征,但从特征仓库查它要几十 ms,而整条链路的特征查询预算只有单位数 ms。
scenario_en: The ranking model wants a feature, but fetching it from the feature store takes tens of ms while the feature-lookup budget is single-digit ms.
q: 面对这个查询太慢的特征，该怎么办？
q_en: What do you do with this too-slow feature?
why: 特征仓库必须在单位数 ms 内供给用户画像/视频元数据;查询超预算的特征只有两条路:提前预计算好存成可快查的形式,或直接从实时模型里丢弃。绝不能让一个慢特征拖垮 sub-100ms 预算。
why_en: The feature store must serve profiles/metadata within single-digit ms, so a feature too slow to fetch has only two options: precompute it into a fast-lookup form, or drop it from the real-time model — never let one slow feature blow the sub-100ms budget.
tradeoff: 预计算(快查但可能不够新鲜) vs 丢弃(省延迟但损失该特征信息)
options: 把整条链路延迟预算放宽到几十 ms 迁就它
预计算成可快查形式,或直接从实时模型丢弃;不能让慢特征拖垮 sub-100ms 预算
在请求时同步现算这个特征,不管多久
给每个用户开一个后台线程慢慢算
options_en: Loosen the whole pipeline's latency budget to tens of ms to accommodate it.
Precompute it into a fast-lookup form, or drop it from the real-time model; never let a slow feature blow the sub-100ms budget.
Compute it synchronously at request time no matter how long it takes.
Spin up a background thread per user to slowly compute it.
whenOtherWins: 若该特征既慢又对精度至关重要,宁可投入把它预计算到近实时(如流式更新到 Redis),而非直接丢弃。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feature is both slow and crucial for accuracy, invest in precomputing it to near-real-time (streamed into Redis) rather than dropping it.
optionExplanations: 放宽端到端预算违背 sub-100ms 这个产品 SLO,一个慢特征不该绑架全局。
对;超预算特征只能预计算或丢弃,这是延迟约束下的标准取舍。
同步现算会直接击穿延迟预算,让整次请求超时。
后台慢算的结果赶不上本次请求,等于这次没有该特征,还平白增复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Loosening the end-to-end budget violates the sub-100ms product SLO; one slow feature should not hold the whole system hostage.
Correct — an over-budget feature can only be precomputed or dropped, the standard tradeoff under a latency constraint.
Computing synchronously blows the latency budget and times out the whole request.
Background slow computation misses this request, so the feature is effectively absent while adding complexity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线服务用户画像/物品元数据的低延迟存储,须在单位数 ms 内返回特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is low-latency online storage for user profiles/item metadata that must return features within single-digit ms.

scenario: 推荐模型用「过去展示并被互动的日志」训练,而这些日志本身就是模型自己之前推荐的结果。
scenario_en: The recommender trains on logs of past impressions and interactions, but those logs are themselves the model's own prior recommendations.
q: 为什么训练-服务偏差是推荐系统的头号失败模式，后果链是什么？
q_en: Why is training-serving skew the dominant failure mode in recsys, and what is the chain?
why: 模型只在自己推荐过的内容上得到反馈→训练数据只覆盖它已经surfacing的东西→强化已推、看不到没推的→质量在无监控时悄悄退化。这就是推荐里训练-服务偏差的自我强化,必须靠监控+探索+负反馈打破。
why_en: The model only gets feedback on what it already recommended, so training data covers only what it surfaced, reinforcing prior recs and never seeing the unshown, and quality silently degrades without monitoring — the self-reinforcing skew broken by monitoring, exploration, and negative feedback.
options: 只在已推内容上得反馈→训练只覆盖已 surfacing 的→强化已推、看不到没推的→无监控时质量悄悄退化
训练数据太多导致过拟合,减少数据即可
只是标签延迟,与自我强化无关
是网络带宽不足造成的偏差
options_en: Feedback only on already-recommended content, so training covers only what was surfaced, reinforcing prior recs and missing the unshown, silently degrading without monitoring.
Too much training data causing overfitting, fixed by reducing data.
Just label delay, unrelated to self-reinforcement.
A skew caused by insufficient network bandwidth.
optionExplanations: 对;推荐日志是模型自造的,只覆盖已推内容,回路自我强化,是训练-服务偏差在 recsys 的典型形态。
过拟合是容量问题,这里是数据覆盖偏差(只见已推),减数据不解决。
标签延迟只是其中一面,本题核心是自我强化的覆盖偏差,不能简化为延迟。
带宽是网络指标,与训练数据的自我强化偏差无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — recommendation logs are self-made and cover only recommended content, so the loop self-reinforces, the classic form of training-serving skew in recsys.
Overfitting is a capacity issue; here it is data-coverage bias (only seeing recommended), which reducing data does not fix.
Label delay is only one facet; the core here is self-reinforcing coverage bias, not reducible to delay.
Bandwidth is a network metric, unrelated to self-reinforcing training-data bias.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐里模型只在自己推过的内容上获得反馈,训练分布被自身历史决策扭曲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In recsys, training-serving skew is the model getting feedback only on what it recommended, so the training distribution is warped by its own past decisions.

scenario: 开场做问题框定,你要覆盖哪些类别的澄清问题,且每个都要能驱动一个下游决策。
scenario_en: Framing at the start, which categories of clarifying questions must you cover, each driving a downstream decision?
q: 视频推荐框定阶段应覆盖哪些澄清类别？(多选)
q_en: Which clarifying-question categories should the framing stage cover? (multiple)
why: 六类各驱动一个下游决策:产品形态(候选策略)、用户类型(CF vs 内容/冷启动)、内容规模(要不要 ANN)、优化目标(标签/损失/护栏)、约束(延迟→实时 vs 预计算)、负反馈(训练含不含负样本)。每问一句都要能落到设计上。
why_en: Six categories each drive a downstream decision: product surface (candidate strategy), user type (CF vs content/cold start), content scale (ANN or not), objective (label/loss/guardrail), constraints (latency to real-time vs precompute), and negative feedback (negatives in training).
options: 产品形态(首页 feed vs watch-next)
用户类型(登录 vs 匿名)与内容规模(目录多大)
优化目标、延迟约束、是否采集负反馈
面试官爱喝什么咖啡
options_en: Product surface (homepage feed vs watch-next).
User type (logged-in vs anonymous) and content scale (catalog size).
Objective, latency constraint, and whether to capture negative feedback.
What coffee the interviewer likes.
optionExplanations: 对;产品形态决定候选生成走宽主题还是上下文锚定。
对;用户类型定 CF vs 内容信号,内容规模定要不要 ANN,都是关键澄清。
对;目标定标签/损失/护栏,延迟定实时 vs 预计算,负反馈定训练含不含负样本。
错;这是闲聊,不驱动任何设计决策,不属于框定问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — product surface decides broad-topic vs context-anchored candidate generation.
Correct — user type sets CF vs content signals and content scale sets whether ANN is needed, both key clarifications.
Correct — objective sets label/loss/guardrail, latency sets real-time vs precompute, negatives set whether training includes them.
Wrong — that is chitchat driving no design decision and is not a framing question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开场用来确定目标/用户/规模/约束的提问,每个都应能驱动一个下游设计决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clarifying question pins down objective/user/scale/constraints up front, each meant to drive a downstream design decision.

q: 把一次视频推荐请求在两阶段架构里的处理顺序排好:
q_en: Order how one video-recommendation request flows through the two-stage architecture:
steps: 候选生成用 ANN 把数十亿视频收窄到数百个(~10-20ms)
排序模型给这数百个候选精细打分(~50-80ms)
按分数取 top 排布最终列表并挂护栏(多样性)
把最终数十条返回给用户展示
why: 顺序是漏斗逐级收窄:先 ANN 候选生成把 billions→hundreds(轻、快),再重排序精打分,然后按分数成列表并挂多样性护栏,最后返回数十条。每一阶段的延迟预算之和必须落在 sub-100ms 内。
why_en: The order is a narrowing funnel: ANN candidate generation cuts billions to hundreds (light, fast), heavy ranking scores them, then top-scored items form the list with a diversity guardrail, and finally dozens are returned — the stage budgets summing under sub-100ms.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  B["数十亿"] --> CG["候选生成 ANN"]
  CG --> H["数百"]
  H --> RK["排序精打分"]
  RK --> L["top+多样性护栏"]
  L --> U["数十条返回"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐的逐级收窄结构:每一层用更重的模型处理更少的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A funnel is the recommendation's progressive narrowing: each layer uses a heavier model on fewer candidates.

scenario: 同一道视频推荐题,L4(中级)和 L5(资深)的区别不在于会更多算法,而在于覆盖广度。
scenario_en: On the same prompt, the L4 (mid) vs L5 (senior) difference is not more algorithms but breadth of coverage.
q: 把 L5 与 L4 拉开差距的，主要是什么？
q_en: What mainly separates L5 from L4 on this question?
why: L5 主动覆盖负反馈、冷启动、多样性等盲区,并给出主指标+护栏且能讲清取舍;L4 只答基础产品+规模、一个主指标。差距在广度与取舍意识,不是更花哨的模型。
why_en: L5 proactively covers blind spots (negative feedback, cold start, diversity) and gives a primary metric plus guardrail with tradeoff reasoning, while L4 answers basic product+scale with one primary metric — the gap is breadth and tradeoff awareness, not fancier models.
tradeoff: L5(主动覆盖盲区+护栏+取舍) vs L4(基础产品/规模+单一主指标)
options: L5 会用更冷门的深度模型架构,L4 不会
L5 主动覆盖负反馈/冷启动/多样性并给主指标+护栏且讲清取舍;L4 只答基础产品/规模+单一指标
L5 写更多代码行数
L5 用更大的 batch size 训练
options_en: L5 uses more obscure deep architectures that L4 does not.
L5 proactively covers negative feedback/cold start/diversity with a primary metric plus guardrail and tradeoff reasoning; L4 answers basic product/scale with one metric.
L5 writes more lines of code.
L5 trains with a bigger batch size.
whenOtherWins: 若题目本身是纯算法深挖(如让你推导 loss),那对具体建模细节的掌握才是区分点;但框定题的分层几乎总看广度与取舍意识。
whenOtherWins_en: If the prompt is a pure algorithm deep-dive (derive the loss), mastery of modeling detail is the differentiator; but for framing questions leveling almost always tracks breadth and tradeoff awareness.
optionExplanations: 分层不看模型花不花哨,用冷门架构不加分,覆盖广度和取舍才是关键。
对;主动覆盖盲区+主指标配护栏+讲清取舍,正是 L5 相对 L4 的分水岭。
代码行数与分层无关,系统设计看的是决策质量不是产量。
batch size 是训练细节,不构成 L4/L5 的能力区分。
optionExplanations_en: Leveling is not about fancy models; obscure architectures earn no credit — coverage breadth and tradeoffs are what count.
Correct — proactively covering blind spots plus a primary metric with a guardrail and clear tradeoffs is exactly the L5-over-L4 divide.
Lines of code are unrelated to leveling; system design tracks decision quality, not output volume.
Batch size is a training detail and does not distinguish L4 from L5 ability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试按候选人覆盖的广度(盲区、取舍、跨系统)而非算法数量来定级别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Level scoping grades a candidate by breadth of coverage (blind spots, tradeoffs, cross-system) rather than number of algorithms.

scenario: Staff+ 级别的回答里,面试官更想听你怎么把「短期参与提升」和「长期留存」区分开,而不只是画一张完美架构图。
scenario_en: At Staff+ level, the interviewer wants how you'd distinguish short-term engagement gains from long-term retention, not just a perfect architecture diagram.
q: 对 Staff+,花两分钟讲清什么，往往比完美架构图更有价值？
q_en: For Staff+, spending two minutes on what often beats a perfect architecture diagram?
why: 讲清 A/B 测试框架如何区分短期参与提升 vs 长期留存:观看时长这类短期指标可能靠标题党刷上去却伤留存,所以要设计能捕捉长期效应的实验(长观察窗、留存/回访指标、holdback 组)。这体现你懂指标会互相打架。
why_en: Explain how the A/B framework distinguishes short-term engagement from long-term retention: watch-time-style short metrics can be gamed by clickbait while hurting retention, so design experiments that capture long-term effects (long windows, retention metrics, holdback groups).
tradeoff: 重 A/B 框架分辨短期 vs 长期(抓住指标冲突) vs 只画完美架构(漏了指标会打架)
options: 多堆几层深度模型的结构图
讲清 A/B 测试框架怎么区分短期参与提升 vs 长期留存(长窗口/留存指标/holdback),体现懂指标冲突
把每个组件的 QPS 都算到小数点后两位
列出所有用过的开源库版本号
options_en: Stack a few more layers of deep-model diagrams.
Explain how the A/B framework distinguishes short-term engagement from long-term retention (long windows/retention metrics/holdback), showing you grasp metric conflict.
Compute each component's QPS to two decimal places.
List version numbers of every open-source library used.
whenOtherWins: 若面试还停在基础架构没搭起来(L4 阶段),那先把两阶段架构讲对更重要;A/B 深挖是架构已清晰后的 Staff+ 加分项。
whenOtherWins_en: If the interview is still at basic architecture (L4 stage), getting the two-stage design right comes first; the A/B deep-dive is a Staff+ bonus once the architecture is clear.
optionExplanations: 堆模型结构图不体现对指标冲突的理解,Staff+ 更看系统级判断。
对;短期 vs 长期的 A/B 设计恰恰暴露指标会打架这一 Staff+ 洞见,常比架构图更值钱。
把 QPS 算到小数点后两位是伪精确,不解决短期长期冲突。
列库版本号与设计判断无关,答不到 Staff+ 想听的取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking model diagrams does not show understanding of metric conflict; Staff+ values system-level judgment.
Correct — short-vs-long A/B design exposes the Staff+ insight that metrics conflict, often worth more than an architecture diagram.
Computing QPS to two decimals is false precision and does not resolve short-vs-long conflict.
Listing library versions is unrelated to design judgment and misses the Staff+ tradeoff they want to hear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组对比不同版本效果;要分辨短期参与与长期留存需长窗口和留存指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users to compare versions; distinguishing short-term engagement from long-term retention needs long windows and retention metrics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期不接受新版本的一小撮用户,用来测量长期(留存)效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A holdback group is a small set of users kept on the old version long-term to measure long-run (retention) effects.

scenario: 复习「商业目标 → ML 指标」的四条映射。
scenario_en: Review the four business-goal to ML-metric mappings.
q: 补全视频推荐的商业目标到 ML 指标映射：
q_en: Fill in the business-goal to ML-metric mappings for video recommendation:
text: 观看时长→预测{{观看时长}}信号;用户满意度→{{NDCG}}(最满意视频是否靠前);内容多样性→{{覆盖率}}+列表内多样性;候选生成阶段→{{Recall@K}}(相关视频有没有被召回)。
text_en: Watch time → predicted {{watch time}} signal; user satisfaction → {{NDCG}} (are the most satisfying videos near the top); content diversity → {{coverage}} + intra-list diversity; candidate generation → {{Recall@K}} (were relevant videos retrieved).
why: 四条映射把商业语言翻成可优化的 ML 指标:时长→预测时长、满意度→NDCG、多样性→覆盖率、候选完整性→Recall@K。记住每条并配一个护栏,是框定的核心产出。
why_en: The four mappings translate business language into optimizable ML metrics: watch time to predicted time, satisfaction to NDCG, diversity to coverage, candidate completeness to Recall@K.

termDefinitions.meaning: 位置加权的排序质量指标,衡量最相关/最满意项是否靠前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a position-weighted ranking-quality metric for whether the most relevant items rank high.

scenario: 只按观看时长排,系统越来越集中推少数头部创作者,长尾创作者拿不到曝光、用户看到的越来越同质。
scenario_en: Ranking purely by watch time concentrates recommendations on a few head creators, starving the long tail of exposure while users see ever more homogeneous content.
q: 为什么要把「多样性」设成护栏，它护住的是什么？
q_en: Why make diversity a guardrail, and what does it protect?
why: 多样性护栏护住创作者生态(长尾也能被曝光,平台供给才健康)和用户体验(防信息茧房)。纯观看时长会向头部集中、窄化推荐;用覆盖率+列表内多样性当护栏,能在追参与的同时不牺牲生态与新鲜感。
why_en: A diversity guardrail protects the creator ecosystem (long-tail creators get exposure so supply stays healthy) and user experience (against filter bubbles), because pure watch time concentrates on head content and narrows recs.
options: 多样性护栏没必要,集中推头部对所有人都最好
多样性护栏护住创作者生态(长尾曝光)+用户体验(防茧房),避免纯观看时长把推荐窄化
多样性只影响存储成本,与生态无关
多样性护栏是为了提高 GPU 利用率
options_en: A diversity guardrail is unnecessary; concentrating on head content is best for everyone.
A diversity guardrail protects the creator ecosystem (long-tail exposure) plus user experience (against bubbles), preventing pure watch time from narrowing recs.
Diversity only affects storage cost, unrelated to the ecosystem.
A diversity guardrail exists to raise GPU utilization.
optionExplanations: 集中推头部会饿死长尾创作者、把用户困进茧房,长期损害平台供给与体验。
对;多样性护栏同时保生态(长尾曝光)和体验(防茧房),是观看时长目标的必要平衡。
多样性关乎曝光分布与生态健康,不是存储成本问题。
GPU 利用率与推荐多样性无关,属无关项。
optionExplanations_en: Concentrating on head content starves long-tail creators and traps users in bubbles, harming platform supply and experience long-term.
Correct — a diversity guardrail protects both the ecosystem (long-tail exposure) and experience (against bubbles), the necessary balance to a watch-time objective.
Diversity concerns exposure distribution and ecosystem health, not storage cost.
GPU utilization is unrelated to recommendation diversity, an irrelevant option.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平台上创作者的整体供给健康度;长尾也需曝光才能持续产出内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The creator ecosystem is the overall supply health of a platform's creators; the long tail also needs exposure to keep producing content.
